title: Positive lifted etale cohomology computed by a finite affine section complex
statement: Let $X$ be a separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $\iota$ a finite set, $U_i$ affine open subsets with $\bigcup_i U_i=X$, and $F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $F_{et}$ be the associated additive sheaf [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module] and let $K=C^\bullet(U,F)$ be its module-valued section Cech complex [def-sc-module-cech-comparison], whose degree $p$ terms are the products of $\Gamma(U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_p},F)$ with alternating restriction differential. Let $T$ forget $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$-module scalars and then apply the additive coefficient lift $\mathrm{ULift}:\mathrm{Ab}_u\to\mathrm{Ab}_{u+1}$. For every $n\ge0$, there exists an additive equivalence $H^{n+1}(X_{et},\mathrm{ULift}(F_{et}))\simeq H^{n+1}(T(K))$. The left group is Ext-defined Sheaf.H, while the right group is homology of the specified lifted section complex. No coefficient-universe comparison of sheaf cohomology is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 03P2, separated-case affine-cover proof; also Proposition 03DW, part (2), separated-case proof. Coefficient lifting of the finite section complex is the worker-written elaboration of that computation.

proof.text: Every nonempty finite intersection of the affine opens is affine because X is separated. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence. The open-immersion pullback/restriction identification and pullback-composition isomorphism identify the associated etale sheaf sections with the sections of F on these intersections, and commute with every restriction map. Apply ULift to these section identifications.

The lifted affine quasi-coherent acyclicity theorem kills every positive cohomology row on these intersections. Apply the Cech-to-derived spectral sequence of the covering in the larger coefficient universe; its degree-zero row computes positive sheaf cohomology. At the terminal object the free-abelian-Yoneda adjunction identifies Hom from the sheafified free representable with evaluation; computing Ext on an injective resolution therefore identifies the H' abutment with right-derived evaluation. Then apply cohomology_nonempty_addEquiv_rightDerived_evaluation_succ to identify this derived evaluation with Ext-defined H. Equivalently, the free representable at the terminal object is the constant integer sheaf. No preservation of injectives by ULift is claimed.

Each Cech degree is a finite product of section groups. Forgetting module scalars and applying ULift preserve these finite products. The section identifications commute with each face restriction, and additivity preserves its sign and the finite alternating sum. They give a complex isomorphism between the etale section complex and the image under forget-scalars followed by ULift of the module section Cech complex. Apply homology to this isomorphism and compose with the edge comparison. This step does not identify the homology with the unlifted cohomology.
